data.title: NexgenRx Announces Third Quarter Results (with Continued Significant Increases in EBITDA, Revenue, and Financial Position)
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / NEXGENRX INC. ("NexgenRx" or the "Company") is pleased to announce its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, with revenues of $4,904,857, income before taxes of $843,735 and EBITDA of $1,048,210, representing significant percentage increases of 8%, 48.8% and 18.1%, respectively, compared to the same period in 2025.

During the quarter, the Company continued to strengthen the foundations of its business and invested in capabilities that will support its next phase of growth. Technology modernization, digital transformation, and process automation remain key priorities as NexgenRx seeks to enhance service quality, improve productivity, and create greater operating efficiencies. In parallel, the Company's Artificial Intelligence ("AI") Committee continued assessing opportunities and has incorporated several AI-based initiatives into the Company's business operations, with a continued emphasis on practical applications that can improve workflow efficiency, strengthen analytical capabilities, and support more informed decision-making. NexgenRx also remain committed to developing its people and organizational capabilities, recognizing that its team's expertise and execution are fundamental to the Company's long-term success.

The Company's third quarter financial results reflect the benefits of these efforts. Revenue grew 8.0% over the comparable quarter in 2025 to $4.9 million, primarily attributable to higher transaction fee revenue resulting from increased transaction volumes and business growth. Gross profit reached $4.2 million. Income before income taxes increased 48.8% to $843,735 from $566,925 in the prior-year period, demonstrating continued improvement in the Company's underlying operating performance. Although NexgenRx achieved a significant growth in pre-tax earnings, the Company recorded a net loss of $63,993 compared to net income of $589,780 in the same period last year. This was directly attributable to income tax expense of $907,728 that the Company chose to recognize in the current quarter, as the Company continues to generate taxable profits and has fully utilized its remaining tax loss carry-forwards. Of this amount, $716,912 represents a non-cash deferred income tax expense arising from the recognition and utilization of deferred tax assets, while the remaining $190,816 represents current income tax expense. EBITDA increased 18.1% to $1.05 million from $887,671 in the prior year period. The growth in EBITDA relative to revenue demonstrates the Company's ability to achieve operating leverage through disciplined cost management and support higher business volumes without a proportionate increase in operating expenses.

The Company's year-to-date performance further reinforces this positive trajectory. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased 13.4% to $15.1 million compared with the corresponding period in 2025. Net income increased 46.7% to $2.2 million, while EBITDA increased 57.9% to $3.70 million. The significant improvement in earnings reflects the combined impact of business expansion, disciplined cost management, and continued operational improvements. The Company believes that these results demonstrate its ability to pursue growth while maintaining a clear focus on profitability and financial discipline.

The Company's financial position also remains strong. As at September 30, 2026, shareholders' equity stood at $8.9 million, reflecting the earnings generated during the year. Cash and cash equivalents totalled $4.1 million, providing financial flexibility to fund day-to-day operations, strategic investments, and future business opportunities, while supporting the Company's ongoing dividend program. Restricted client funds held on deposit amounted to $29.6 million, consistent with the scale of the Company's client relationships and transaction processing activities. Together, the Company's financial resources and disciplined capital management provide a sound platform for continued investment and growth.

Ron Loucks, President and CEO, stated "The Company delivered a solid performance in the third quarter of 2026, continuing to advance our strategic priorities while maintaining a strong focus on profitable growth and operational execution. Third quarter results demonstrate the strength and scalability of our business model, supported by sustained client demand, growing transaction activity, and our ability to translate business expansion into improved financial performance. Looking ahead, our priorities remain firmly centred on sustainable expansion, operational excellence, and long-term value creation. We will continue to allocate resources toward technology, AI-enabled capabilities, and automation, while pursuing opportunities to deepen client relationships, strengthen our competitive position, and expand our market presence. We remain disciplined in evaluating growth opportunities and committed to balancing investment with financial performance. With a strong financial foundation, an experienced and dedicated team, and a clear strategic direction, we are confident in our ability to build on the progress achieved in 2026 and create enduring value for our shareholders."

About NexgenRx

NexgenRx is Canada's only independent full-service Third-Party Administrator and Technology Solutions Provider, offering proprietary full front-end, eligibility, enrolment, hour bank and mobile access capabilities, together with state-of-the-art claims adjudication and full provider network coverage. These combined capabilities allow NexgenRx to provide Plan Sponsors, sophisticated administration and health benefit technology applications in a cost-effective SaaS (Software as a Service) Model.

NexgenRx is committed to building partnerships with organizations looking to exceed the expectations of their clients and plan members and deliver superior administration and claims processing solutions at a competitive cost. More information on NexgenRx can be found at www.nexgenrx.com.

data.title: Intuit Selling Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion to Berkshire Hathaway-Backed Bending Spoons — Update
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Intuit has agreed to sell its email automation platform Mailchimp for $3.68 billion to Bending Spoons, the owner of several wayward tech brands that recently attracted a major investment from Berkshire Hathaway.

The purchase price includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in Bending Spoons stock.

The deal comes about a month after Bending Spoons revealed that Berkshire Hathaway had invested about $930 million in the company, accumulating a 4% stake. The Milan-based company said at the time the investment would provide fresh funds to pursue additional acquisitions.

Mailchimp joins an eclectic stable of digital brands Bending Spoons owns including AOL, Everbrite, Evernote, Vimeo and others. Bending Spoons Chief Executive Luca Ferrari said his company, which went public in July, plans to invest substantially in Mailchimp once the deal closes.

Intuit said selling Mailchimp would allow it to focus on its core products, including Quickbooks, Credit Karma and TurboTax, where it is implementing more AI features. The company plans to use cash proceeds to buy back shares during fiscal 2027.

"It's better for our focus, better for our capital allocation," Chief Executive Sasan Goodarzi said on a call with investors.

The deal, which is expected to close early in 2027, came as both companies released their quarterly earnings.

Intuit reported a higher profit as revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion in its fiscal first quarter, with results topping analyst estimates. Sales in Intuit's business-facing segment increased 15%, while its consumer-facing sales rose 7%.

Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million in the quarter.

For the full year, Intuit said it now expected revenue between $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, down from its prior view for $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. It expects earnings per share of $20.12 to $20.36.

For the current second quarter, Intuit projected revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion, with earnings per share between $2.55 and $2.60. Both projections were below analysts' estimates of $5.11 billion in sales and $3.73 a share in earnings.

Bending Spoons, meanwhile, raised its outlook for the year, after reporting higher profit and revenue in the third quarter.

Shares of Intuit fell almost 10% in late trading to $297.25, while shares of Bending Spoons rose 4.3% to $43.50.

data.title: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Approves Five Energy Projects
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved five energy projects and facilities on Thursday in its effort to clear the way for critical natural gas infrastructure projects.

The approved projects include Sabine Pass's authority to operate three additional liquefaction trains at an existing terminal in Cameron Parish, La.

The commission has also issued Mountain Valley Pipeline a certificate to operate a project in Virginia and West Virginia to add 600,000 dekatherms per day of firm transportation capacity.

The approvals include a southeast Virginia energy storage project, a building certificate for the Forza Pipeline in New Mexico and Texas, and then an expansion of Texas Eastern's projects in Mississippi.

data.title: States Move to Block Disney's Bid for Character.ai Assets — WSJ
data.description:
By Akiko Matsuda

A coalition of roughly 40 U.S. states filed an objection to bankrupt chatbot maker Character Technologies' proposed deal with Disney, arguing the transaction would benefit departing insiders and threaten consumer privacy.

The state attorneys general said in a Wednesday filing in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del., that the deal is designed to "lock in" arrangements Disney made with Character before the bankruptcy filing and potentially transfer the private conversations of users of the Character.ai chatbot, including minors.

Under the proposed deal, Disney would pay $20 million for a nonexclusive license to use Character's intellectual property and artificial intelligence technology. The offer serves as a stalking horse bid, setting a floor price that can be topped by others at a court-supervised auction.

The bid excludes sensitive personal information such as raw user chat histories, but the states argued that what Disney plans to license — for example, AI models — is built on years of real consumer conversations and mental-health disclosures made by users while using the app. They asserted that the transaction should be scrutinized because many states prohibit the sale of that type of personal information.

A spokesperson for Disney didn't return a request for comment on Thursday.

In September, a month before Character filed for bankruptcy, Disney hired 66 of Character's 86 employees, including former Chief Executive Karandeep Anand, while obtaining legal releases protecting itself and those employees, the states said in the filing. The states said the prebankruptcy transaction is worth roughly $180 million in compensation and retention over three years.

The states said Disney retained the workforce, secured broad legal releases and dictated bidding procedures before the bankruptcy filing, so the transaction demands "heightened scrutiny."

Texas, in a separate filing, joined the coalition's objection, challenging that the transaction would block states from pursuing existing civil investigations into Character's practices.

The raw personal data collected by Character's chatbot platform has drawn a separate stalking horse bidder from an entity tied to Kai McPheeters, a co-founder of game developer Yonder. The states expressed concern over the proposed deal during a recent court hearing.

The states' pushback against Character's deal mirrors a wider fight over personal data privacy in corporate restructurings. Earlier this week, a New York judge approved Alphabet's acquisition of employee data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines after the Google parent company agreed to provide additional privacy protections.

Write to Akiko Matsuda at akiko.matsuda@wsj.com

data.title: TPG to take BILL Holdings private in $6 billion deal
data.description:
Fintech firm BILL Holdings said on Thursday it will be acquired by private equity group TPG, in partnership with Corpay , in an all-cash transaction valued at about $6 billion.

BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average share price through November 16, the last full trading day before BILL takeover talks were reported.

The company was valued at a little under $5 billion before the media reports. Its shares fell about 3% in aftermarket trading.

Corpay is set to invest $1.10 billion in the fintech firm as part of the take-private deal, which would be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027.

BILL provides cloud-based software that helps small and midsize businesses automate financial operations, including accounts payable and receivable.

Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners were serving as financial advisors to BILL.

data.title: Foreign banks keep buying into India
data.description:
Fairfax Financial sold its whole stake in Indian lender IIFL Finance for about $370mn on November 18, raising cash for its $5.66bn takeover of state-controlled IDBI Bank.

The Canadian insurer's unit FIH Mauritius Investments offered more than 56mn shares at a floor price of INR611 ($6.54), 3.9% below the previous close, The Times of India reported. The block was worth about INR34.54bn, a person with direct knowledge of the trade told Reuters, and IIFL Finance shares climbed as much as 6.5% on the day.

Money is moving across Asia's borders into banks, and most of it is heading for India. In the same two days Japan's Daiwa Securities Group set out plans to grow in China and South Korea's Kakao Bank bought into a Mongolian lender. Both are spending profits earned in unusually strong home markets.

Foreign stakes in Indian lenders, deal value, $bn. Rupee values converted at November 18, 2026 ECB reference rates. Source: Government of India; Emirates NBD and RBL Bank; Reuters; The Indian Express. IntelliNews

A strike that did not stop the sale

New Delhi's Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on October 15 cleared the sale of 60.72% of IDBI Bank to a Canadian subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings for INR528.78bn, or INR81 a share. The government is selling 30.48% and Life Insurance Corporation of India 30.24%, and officials expect the deal to be the biggest foreign direct investment yet in India's financial sector. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must still judge the buyer fit and proper.

IDBI's staff unions want the deal scrapped. The United Forum of IDBI Officers & Employees held a two-day nationwide strike on November 2 and 3, calling the valuation inadequate and the process opaque, the Indo-Asian News Service reported. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has argued that the sale breaches RBI rules limiting a foreign owner to 26% of the voting rights in an Indian bank.

The queue of foreign buyers

Fairfax would be the largest of several foreign buyers. Emirates NBD took 60% of RBL Bank on June 18 through a primary share issue worth about $2.75bn, which the two lenders described as the first purchase of a majority stake in a profitable Indian bank by a foreign bank, according to their joint statement. The Dubai bank's own Indian branches merge into RBL on December 1.

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp paid INR134.83bn for 20% of Yes Bank, and Bank of America agreed in August to take up to 49.9% of Jio Credit, the lending arm of Jio Financial Services, for as much as INR182.68bn.

The books these buyers are paying for are much cleaner than a decade ago. Non-performing loans at Indian banks fell to 2.1% of gross loans in 2025 from 10% in 2017, according to World Bank data.

Indian banks' non-performing loans, % of gross loans. Source: World Bank (IMF Financial Soundness Indicators) via IntelliNews Lambda

Japan and Korea push outwards

Daiwa intends to expand cross-border M&A, listings and advisory work in China now that it owns all of its mainland securities venture, Nikkei Asia reported on November 18. Daiwa agreed in April to buy the 49% held by two Beijing state-owned partners for CNY706mn, Bloomberg reported at the time. 'We are the only Japanese brokerage with an investment banking license in China,' Zhu Hongxia, Daiwa's deputy head for Asia and Oceania, told the newspaper.

In Seongnam, south of Seoul, Kakao Bank on November 17 signed for 15% of M Bank, the digital lender of Mongolian conglomerate MCS Group, and became its second-largest shareholder. No price was disclosed. Mongolia is the Korean internet bank's third foreign market, after a stake in Indonesia's Superbank in 2023 and a holding in Thailand's planned virtual lender Bank X.

Paid for at home

Japan's three megabanks all raised their targets for the year to March 2027 on November 13. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group lifted its net profit goal to JPY2.8 trillion ($17.5bn) from JPY2.7 trillion and authorised a buyback of up to JPY200bn. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group raised its forecast to JPY1.9 trillion ($11.9bn) from JPY1.7 trillion and added a JPY220bn repurchase. Mizuho Financial Group now expects JPY1.6 trillion, up from JPY1.4 trillion.

Each figure is above the record each group earned in the year to March 2026, when MUFG made JPY2.43 trillion, SMFG JPY1.58 trillion and Mizuho JPY1.25 trillion. Higher domestic interest rates have widened lending margins, and the groups are fighting over wealthy clients at home as well.

Japan's megabanks, net profit attributable to owners of parent, JPY trillion. Source: MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho results filings. IntelliNews

Those earnings, and the Gulf's, give lenders the capital to keep shopping abroad, and India remains the main destination. Whether the IDBI strike and the political objections can slow the flow will become clearer once the RBI rules on Fairfax.

This article was produced with the help of the IntelliNews Lambda analytical tool

data.title: Molson Coors Beverage Company Announces Regular Quarterly Dividend
data.description:
The Board of Directors of Molson Coors Beverage Company (, TAP.A) today declared a regular quarterly dividend on its Class A and Class B common stock of US$0.48 per share, payable December 18, 2026, to stockholders of record on December 4, 2026. The quarterly dividend is payable to holders of Class A and Class B common stock of Molson Coors Beverage Company.

In addition, the Board of Directors of Molson Coors Canada Inc. (TSX: TPX.B, TPX.A) today declared a quarterly dividend of approximately CAD$0.68 (the Canadian dollar equivalent of the dividend declared on Molson Coors Beverage Company stock), payable December 18, 2026, to its Class A and Class B exchangeable shareholders of record on December 4, 2026. The dividends declared in respect of the Class A and Class B exchangeable shares are eligible dividends for Canadian tax purposes.

OVERVIEW OF MOLSON COORS BEVERAGE COMPANY

For more than two centuries, we have brewed beverages that unite people to celebrate all life’s moments. From our core power brands, Coors Light, Miller Lite, Coors Banquet, Molson Canadian, Carling and Ožujsko to our above premium brands, including Madrí Excepcional, Staropramen, Blue Moon Belgian White and Leinenkugel’s Summer Shandy, to our value brands, like Miller High Life and Keystone Light, we produce many beloved and iconic beers. While our history is rooted in beer, we offer a modern portfolio that expands beyond the beer aisle as well, including flavored beverages like Vizzy Hard Seltzer and Monaco, spirits and non-alcoholic beverages. We also have partner brands, such as Simply Spiked, ZOA Energy, Fever-Tree, among others, through license, distribution, partnership and joint venture agreements. As a business, our ambition is to be the first choice for our people, our consumers and our customers, and our success depends on our ability to make our products available to meet a wide range of consumer segments and occasions.

To learn more about Molson Coors Beverage Company, visit molsoncoors.com.

ABOUT MOLSON COORS CANADA INC.

Molson Coors Canada Inc. ("MCCI") is a subsidiary of Molson Coors Beverage Company. MCCI Class A and Class B exchangeable shares offer substantially the same economic and voting rights as the respective classes of common shares of MCBC, as described in MCBC’s annual proxy statement and Form 10-K filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The trustee holder of the special Class A voting stock and the special Class B voting stock has the right to cast a number of votes equal to the number of then outstanding Class A exchangeable shares and Class B exchangeable shares, respectively.
